question: In A/Gb mode, a cell may be reserved for exclusive access by SoLSA. How can an MS camp normally on such a cell? [3GPP Release 18]
options: By having a special access code
By having a specific PLMN subscription
By having a higher priority than other MS
By having a Localised Service Area subscription to the cell
correct_answer: By having a Localised Service Area subscription to the cell

question: What is the meaning of MPS-subscribed UE?
options: A UE with a personal identification number
A UE that utilizes virtual private networks
A UE that has a subscription to a mobile network operator supporting MPS
A UE that utilizes over-the-top services
A UE with multimedia telephony capabilities
correct_answer: A UE that has a subscription to a mobile network operator supporting MPS

question: What is the function of the LCS Client? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To provide location information for target UEs
To perform positioning of target UEs
To request location information for target UEs
To serve as a platform for location-based services
To determine the services provided by the LCS server
correct_answer: To request location information for target UEs

question: What are the two types of reference points for SAN type 1-H? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Radiated and conducted reference points
Operating band specific radiated interface and conducted reference points
Transceiver array boundary and satellite payload
Radio distribution network and antenna array
correct_answer: Radiated and conducted reference points

question: What does the low-frequency upturn in the U-shaped S-F curve indicate? [IEEE C95.1]
options: The modification of the cell's resting potential due to depolarization.
The initiation of nerve excitation at a zero crossing of the sinusoidal waveform.
The slow rate of rise of the sinusoid allowing the nerve to accommodate to the stimulus.
The dependence of the induced field on the derivative of the environmental field.
The convergence of thresholds to a slope proportional to frequency for continued sinusoidal stimulation.
correct_answer: The slow rate of rise of the sinusoid allowing the nerve to accommodate to the stimulus.

question: In a GERAN based MOCN configuration, when does a cell with closed/hybrid access need to coordinate the CSG IDs between the operators' PLMNs? [3GPP Release 17]
options: When the cell broadcasts several PLMN IDs
When the cell broadcasts a CSG ID
When the cell broadcasts several CSG IDs
When the cell switches between closed access and hybrid access
When the cell switches between broadcast control channel and synchronization channel
correct_answer: When the cell broadcasts several PLMN IDs

question: What actions should the AP or PCP take if it receives DMG Beacon frames with the ECAPC Policy Enforced field set to 1 and the Cluster Member Role set to 1? [IEEE 802.11]
options: Remain unclustered
Join a selected S-AP as a cluster coordinator
Join a different BSS as a cluster member
Join a selected S-AP as a cluster member
correct_answer: Join a selected S-AP as a cluster member

question: What does a UE expect when it cancels a PUSCH or an SRS transmission? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To be scheduled by a second DCI format for transmission over symbols that include cancelled symbols
To continue the cancelled transmission after a corresponding symbol
To transmit another PUSCH or SRS over symbols that include cancelled symbols
To be scheduled by a second DCI format for transmission over symbols that do not include cancelled symbols
None of the above
correct_answer: To be scheduled by a second DCI format for transmission over symbols that include cancelled symbols

Modularity
Standardization
Data exchange
Augmented reality

question: What are the major challenges of signal detection in mMTC (massive machine type communication)?
options: Active use detection (AUD)
Channel estimation (CE)
Multi-user data detection
All of the above
None of the above

question: What functionalities does the Edge Application Server Discovery Function (EASDF) include? [3GPP Release 18]
options: Registering to NRF for EASDF discovery and selection
Handling DNS messages from the UE
Forwarding DNS messages to C-DNS or L-DNS for DNS Query
Providing a DNS response with a specific IP address to a DNS query
All of the above
correct_answer: All of the above

question: According to IEEE Std 802.11-2020, what should a STA do if it is unable to transmit a buffered BU during the beacon interval? [IEEE 802.11]
options: Discard the buffered BU
Announce the BU again by transmitting an ATIM frame
Transmit BUs without announcement to STAs known to be in the awake state
Transmit an ACK frame to the AP
Transition into PS mode
correct_answer: Announce the BU again by transmitting an ATIM frame

question: What is the definition of authenticator address (AA)?
options: The medium access control (MAC) address of the IEEE 802.1X Authenticator’s STA.
An entity that provides an authentication service to an Authenticator.
The service used to establish the identity of one station (STA) as a member of the set of STAs authorized to associate with another STA.
The act of determining whether a particular right, such as access to a resource, is granted to an entity.
The horizontal orientation of the front surface of a station or of a radio antenna system’s main lobe measured clockwise from true north.
correct_answer: The medium access control (MAC) address of the IEEE 802.1X Authenticator’s STA.

question: What is the scope of the CH14-SMST4 Charging Work Item? [3GPP Release 14]
options: Charging for SMS from MME
Charging for SMS-SC deliveries using T4 functionalities
Charging for Device Triggering services
Charging for MSISDN-less MO-SMS via T4 functionalities
Charging for Proximity-based services

question: What is the purpose of ADRF in the 5G system architecture? [3GPP Release 18]
options: To interact with different entities for data collection
To provide analytics to consumers
To store and retrieve collected data and analytics
To exchange input data or data analytics between PLMNs
To request and subscribe to trained ML model provisioning services

question: What is the function of the Serving GPRS Support Node (SGSN)? [3GPP Release 17]
options: To provide support for handovers between 3GPP access networks.
To terminate the interface towards the PDN.
To control the circuit switched services to and from mobile stations.
To perform switching and signaling functions for mobile stations.
To handle packet transmission to and from mobile stations.
correct_answer: To handle packet transmission to and from mobile stations.

question: What key is used to generate the Challenge Text in shared-key authentication? [IEEE 802.11]
options: The WEP initialization vector
The shared key distributed to stations
The MAC address of the mobile station
The WEP keystream generated with a random key and initialization vector
correct_answer: The WEP keystream generated with a random key and initialization vector

question: What is the definition of 5GMM-CONNECTED mode?
options: A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE is connected to the 5G core network via 3GPP access.
A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE is connected to the 5G core network via non-3GPP access.
A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE can be either in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over 3GPP access or in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over non-3GPP access.
A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE is not connected to any access network.
A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE is not registered with any PLMN or SNPN.
correct_answer: A UE in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode means the UE can be either in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over 3GPP access or in 5GMM-CONNECTED mode over non-3GPP access.

question: What is the definition of DSM in the context of IEEE Std 802.11-2020?
options: A class of coordination function used in specific service sets (SSs)
A function within an access point (AP) that provides access between the distribution system (DS) and the wireless medium (WM)
A system used to interconnect a set of basic service sets (BSSs) and integrated local area networks (LANs)
The medium or set of media used by a distribution system (DS) for communications between access points (APs), mesh gates, and the portal of an extended service set (ESS)

The set of services provided by the distribution system (DS) that enable the medium access control (MAC) to transport MAC service tuples between stations (STAs) that are not in direct communication with each other over a single instance of the wireless medium (WM)
correct_answer: The medium or set of media used by a distribution system (DS) for communications between access points (APs), mesh gates, and the portal of an extended service set (ESS)

question: What is the Base Station RF bandwidth?

question: What is the purpose of transform precoding in the physical uplink shared channel? [3GPP Release 17]

To enhance the orthogonality of the transmitted symbols.
